source_read: PMC full text PMC1931610 (published PLoS ONE version) in the reader's own browser tab: abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, every Materials and Methods subsection, figure legends, acknowledgments, competing-interest and funding statements, and the reference list. Paragraph structure checked in the page DOM (Results 7 paragraphs, Discussion 6). Figures 1-6 were not needed: every value checked is printed in the text. Card check only (no claims in the task); the source was read in full before the card was opened.

key_findings.correction: Note: 'as quickly as' follows Results, 3rd paragraph, and the non-significant comparison F(14,700)=0.41. The Discussion's 5th paragraph instead says the both-rewarded rats got there more rapidly (significant from day 2 vs day 7); see missed.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently. Across the both-rewarded experiments with stated percentages, 3 of 78 rats preferred cocaine (1/43 naive, 2/24 reversal, 0/11 escalated): 96% did not. Neither this nor any other combination gives 94%.

Results, 1st paragraph, says the extra rats in the cocaine-only and both-rewarded conditions served the dose, delay, effort, reversal, calorie and thirst experiments, so the Figure 2 groups probably came from those conditions. Even so, the named groups (82 + 11 escalated + 10 intoxicated = 103) do not reach the 112 analysed. Allocation cannot be reconstructed either way.

Degrees of freedom checked: F(28,1106) gives 82 rats, F(14,700) 52, t(50) 52, F(40,1160) 30, F(40,1680) 43 and F(20,1000) 52, all matching the printed group sizes. So the printed sizes are after exclusion, and 16 of 46 (35%) cocaine-only rats vs 4 of 47 (8.5%) both-rewarded rats were excluded.

risk_of_bias.note: SYRCLE overall high (editors' summary). Item 1 'high' is justified by the fixed ascending order of the within-animal tests (dose, delay, cost; no fluid, water, saccharin), which the Methods and the Figure 2 legend state; between-group allocation alone would be 'unclear'. Item 8 'high' is right given outcome-related, uneven exclusion. Animal findings are labelled as such throughout, and doses appear only as study conditions, with no human-equivalent dose.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: 'clearly demonstrate' and 'drug-sensitized and -addicted individuals' rest on escalated intake alone. The human extensions (supernormal stimuli; sugar as a 'shield' against drug addiction) are speculation.

missed: Internal inconsistency: Results, 3rd paragraph, says the both-rewarded rats acquired the saccharin preference as quickly as the saccharin-only rats. Discussion, 5th paragraph, says they did so more rapidly (significant from day 2 vs day 7) and puts this down to cocaine's ambivalent effects. Minor.

Design detail: sampling always ran cocaine lever first (C-S-C-S), chosen to prevent drug-induced taste aversion (Materials and Methods › Discrete-trials choice procedure), so each saccharin sample followed a cocaine infusion. The fixed order is part of the procedure the result is tied to.
Results, 6th paragraph: 'This increase was not sufficient' refers to the decrease in saccharin choice with delay. A wording slip with no effect on the finding.
